claim: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight looped transformer.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token.

claim: The 26.4-billion-parameter model runs middle layers three times per token with a 20 GB footprint.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping.
The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers.

claim: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini on November 20, 2026, a 26.4-billion-parameter model looping 12 middle layers three times per token.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini runs 12 of its 24 layers three times in a row.

claim: The model is released under Apache 2.0 with text and image inputs and a 1-million-token context window.

support.quote: It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, with text and image input and a 1M token context window.

claim: The model's 24 physical layers include 3.4 billion active parameters per pass and 5.4 billion activations per token across three loops.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each.
Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping.

claim: Most weights were trained in NVFP4 with final four layers in MXFP8, resulting in roughly 20 GB memory footprint.

support.quote: Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8.
The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers.

claim: The model runs offline on consumer laptops, supporting Mac systems with 32 GB RAM via Ollama and NVIDIA DGX Spark.

support.quote: The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers.
At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama.

claim: Researchers ran the model offline on a MacBook Pro during a flight to build a playable flight simulator.

support.quote: The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers.

claim: The model divides 24 layers into four six-layer blocks and uses attention residuals for cross-loop message passing.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each.
The second and third passes through the middle blocks also read the middle blocks’ outputs from the previous pass, which we call the message.

claim: Looping the middle 12 layers beat looping the last 12 layers on 27 of 28 evaluations.

support.quote: looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

claim: Thinking Machines Lab pruned two-thirds of experts during midtraining to retain 128 most-used expert blocks per layer.

support.quote: At a single point during midtraining, we pruned two-thirds of the experts, leaving the 128 experts that were most used in each layer.

claim: Tokens route to 8 of 128 experts, while hybrid attention pairs 1,024-token local windows with global attention every six layers.

support.quote: Inside each layer, the model uses sparse mixture-of-experts routing: 128 expert blocks exist, but each token is routed to only 8 of them.

Attention is a hybrid of local layers, which mostly attend to the last 1,024 tokens, and global layers (every sixth layer) that attend to the full context, which is how the model supports a 1 million token context window without every layer paying full quadratic attention cost.

claim: Inkling 2 Mini leads open models under 100 billion parameters on DeepSWE v1.1 at 48.2% and Vals Index v2.2 at 46.5%.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%).

claim: Artificial Analysis placed the model at 20 on its Intelligence Index matching Qwen3.8 27B and Nanbeige4.3-33B with fewer active parameters.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini matches Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) and Nanbeige4.3-33B on the Intelligence Index with ~5x and ~6x fewer active parameters, respectively.

claim: Inkling 2 Mini used 38% more output tokens than Qwen3.8 27B but 2.8 times less compute, costing $0.59 and 9.0 minutes vs $3.53 and 38.2 minutes.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini uses ~38% more output tokens than Qwen3.8 27B for the same Intelligence Index score, but ~2.8x less compute.
It costs $0.59 and takes 9.0 minutes per Intelligence Index task vs. $3.53 and 38.2 minutes for Qwen3.8 27B.

claim: Looping does not increase factual recall, which depends primarily on total parameter count.

support.quote: While looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count.

claim: The model scored -8.6 on AA-Omniscience factuality and led on search benchmarks such as BrowseComp and DeepSearchQA.

support.quote: Inkling 2 Mini’s score on AA-Omniscience, a measure of factuality, is in line with other models of the same size.
Inkling 2 Mini overcomes the knowledge gap by efficiently using search and tools. It leads open-weights models of similar size on BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and MCP Atlas.

claim: In independent testing by MindStudio, the model looped for over an hour trying to debug a calculation error.

support.quote: In one independent test, the model looped for over an hour trying to debug a tiered pricing calculation error without reaching a fix, despite scoring well on standardized coding benchmarks.

claim: The model card states that Inkling 2 Mini is not strongly multilingual and performs best in English.

support.quote: the model card itself states it is not strongly multilingual and performs best in English

claim: Thinking Machines Lab released a variable-loop research variant on Hugging Face to study chain-of-thought monitoring.

support.quote: The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three.
Inkling 2 Mini runs 12 of its 24 layers three times in a row.

claim: Reasoning at 5 passes averaged 1,661 tokens compared with 3,703 at 1 pass, while sentence length and word rates remained unchanged.

support.quote: Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged.

claim: Reasoning time horizon rose from 16 to 37 seconds with loops, showing no upward trend on tests of agentic sabotage.

support.quote: The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three.
The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

claim: Thinking Machines Lab provided Goodfire with early access to weights to investigate internal mechanisms.

support.quote: Thinking Machines provided Goodfire with early access to the weights of Inkling 2 Mini so we could investigate how these architectural innovations affect the model’s internal mechanisms.

claim: Goodfire reported that looped layers coordinate across passes, and models are available via Tinker and Hugging Face.

support.quote: November 20, 2026

Our preliminary findings include insights into how layers coordinate with each other, and with future and past versions of themselves: counterintuitively, looped model layers can write to themselves, or read from “future” layers!

claim: Thinking Machines Lab acknowledged that Inkling 2 Mini trails Qwen3.8-27B on MultiChallenge (50.0%) and ComplexConstraints v1.1 (33.4%).

support.quote: it scores 50.0% on MultiChallenge and 33.4% on ComplexConstraints v1.1, behind Qwen3.8-27B on both.

claim: MindStudio reported that looping and per-pass memory add real inference latency, yielding slower token generation speeds.

support.quote: The tradeoff, as observed in independent testing, is that the looping and per-pass memory add real inference latency.

claim: Non-looping models cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute on 512k traces.

support.quote: The non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute to match the looped version’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces.
